calls.summary: Create a Jira issue (REST v3).

params.notes: Method and path come from the Jira rate limiting page, which prices this call. The request body wasn't readable (reference page JS-rendered, OpenAPI cut off), so its fields are left out rather than guessed. Fill from the reference page or the createmeta endpoint.

auth.notes: Basic auth needs an API token; passwords are deprecated. Build email:api_token, base64 it, send it as Basic. OAuth 2.0 scopes aren't confirmed, so none are listed.

config.generic:
# Body shape unconfirmed; see notes.
curl -s -u "$ATLASSIAN_EMAIL:$ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN" -X POST \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue -d @issue.json

rate_limit.notes: Costs 1 point against the hourly quota. Writes to one issue are also capped at 20 per 2 seconds and 100 per 30 seconds. Default POST burst limit is 100 requests per second.

errors.meaning: A rate limit was exceeded. RateLimit-Reason says which; Retry-After gives the seconds to wait.
errors.fix: Atlassian says to retry only idempotent calls. Creating an issue isn't idempotent, so check whether it was created before retrying.

errors.meaning: Sent in the X-Seraph-LoginReason header when CAPTCHA was triggered for the account. Basic auth won't work until it's cleared.
errors.fix: Sign in to Jira in a browser and complete the CAPTCHA, then retry.

smoke.notes: No request defined until the body is confirmed. Point it at a test project.

errors.meaning: A rate limit was exceeded. RateLimit-Reason says which (jira-quota-global-based, jira-quota-tenant-based, jira-burst-based, jira-per-issue-on-write). Retry-After gives the seconds to wait.
errors.fix: Wait at least Retry-After seconds, then back off exponentially with jitter. Atlassian says to retry only idempotent calls that came back with Retry-After.

errors.meaning: Sent in the X-Seraph-LoginReason header when CAPTCHA was triggered for the account. Basic auth to the REST API won't work until it's cleared.
errors.fix: Sign in to Jira in a browser and complete the CAPTCHA, then retry.

errors.seen_in: Claude, Matt's work org, GitHub MCP server
errors.needs_info: Is the setting Matt uses on the Claude side (a show-UI toggle) or this server flag? Confirm the exact name, then mark verified.

smoke.notes: Creates a real event. Use a test calendar ID and sendUpdates=none.

calls.summary: List events on a calendar, optionally in a time window.

params.notes: calendarId "primary" is the signed-in user's main calendar. Use singleEvents=true to expand recurring events (needed for orderBy=startTime).

calls.body: orderBy=startTime only works with singleEvents=true, per the orderBy enum description in the discovery doc.

calls.summary: Get the latest version of a Google Doc as structured JSON.

params.notes: With includeTabsContent=true, content comes back in Document.tabs instead of body. Docs with tabs need this to see every tab.

calls.summary: List or search the user's Drive files.

params.notes: pageSize max 1000. For shared drives set supportsAllDrives=true and includeItemsFromAllDrives=true. fields is a standard Google query parameter for partial responses.

auth.notes: drive.file only sees files the app created or the user opened with it.

calls.summary: Create a draft (gets the DRAFT label). Safer default than sending.

params.notes: Body is a Draft resource whose message.raw is a base64url-encoded RFC 2822 email.

config.generic:
RAW=$(printf 'To: you@example.com\r\nSubject: Test draft\r\n\r\nHello' | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\n')
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"message\":{\"raw\":\"$RAW\"}}" \
  "https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/drafts"

smoke.notes: Creates a real draft. Run only against a test mailbox.

calls.body: The raw-message format (base64url RFC 2822) comes from the Message schema's raw field in the discovery doc.

calls.summary: Get one message by ID, in minimal, full, raw or metadata format.

params.notes: format is one of minimal, full, raw, metadata. metadataHeaders only applies with format=metadata.

calls.summary: List message IDs in the user's mailbox, optionally filtered by a Gmail search query.

params.notes: userId accepts "me" for the authenticated user. maxResults defaults to 100, max 500. q uses Gmail search box syntax. Returns IDs only; call messages.get for content.

auth.notes: The discovery doc lists gmail.metadata, but per the q description the q parameter can't be used with the metadata scope. Use gmail.readonly if you search.

calls.body: Response shape (ListMessagesResponse) is from the discovery doc. Field names in the example are from that schema; values are placeholders.

calls.summary: Append rows after the last row of the table found in a range.

params.notes: valueInputOption is RAW or USER_ENTERED. The method description says the caller must give spreadsheet ID, range and valueInputOption, though the parameter itself isn't flagged required.

smoke.notes: Writes real rows. Use a scratch spreadsheet.

calls.summary: Read a range of cell values (A1 or R1C1 notation).

params.notes: URL-encode the range, e.g. Sheet1!A1:D10 becomes Sheet1%21A1%3AD10.

calls.summary: Post a message to a channel, DM or thread.

params.notes: Pass the token as a Bearer header. markdown_text max 12,000 chars; keep text under 4,000. Use thread_ts to reply in a thread.

auth.notes: Same scope for bot and user tokens. Bots need chat:write.public to post in public channels they haven't joined. Bots can't post into a DM between two users.

config.generic:
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d '{"channel":"C0123456789","text":"Hello from the registry"}'

rate_limit.notes: Generally about 1 message per second per channel.

errors.meaning: Cannot post user messages to a channel they are not in.
errors.fix: Invite the bot to the channel, or add chat:write.public for public channels.

errors.meaning: Value passed for channel was invalid.
errors.fix: Use the channel ID (C..., G..., D...), not the name.

errors.meaning: The token is not granted the scope this call needs.
errors.fix: Add chat:write to the app and reinstall it to the workspace.

smoke.notes: Posts a real message. Use a private test channel the bot is in.

calls.summary: Edit a message the same token posted.

params.notes: Only messages posted by the same authenticated user or bot can be updated. Ephemeral messages can't be updated.

config.generic:
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d '{"channel":"C0123456789","ts":"1700000000.000100","text":"Edited"}'

errors.meaning: The authenticated user doesn't have permission to update this message.
errors.fix: Update with the same token that posted it.

errors.meaning: No message exists with that timestamp.
The workspace's edit settings don't allow editing this message any more.

smoke.notes: Edits a real message. Pair with a postMessage in a test channel.

calls.summary: Read the message history of a channel or DM.

params.notes: limit default 100, max 999; Slack recommends 200 or fewer. Paginate with response_metadata.next_cursor.

auth.notes: Pick the scope for the conversation type (public, private, DM, group DM). Bot tokens only reach conversations the bot is a member of.

errors.meaning: The token doesn't have access to the channel. Only user tokens can read public channels they aren't in.
errors.fix: Invite the bot, or use a user token.

errors.meaning: Value passed for channel was invalid.
The token is not granted the scope this call needs.
errors.fix: Add the history scope for that conversation type and reinstall.

errors.meaning: The request was rate limited.
errors.fix: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then retry.

calls.summary: Read the replies in one thread.

params.notes: ts is the parent message timestamp. limit default 1000; Slack recommends 200 or fewer. reply_users can hold bot IDs, not only user IDs.

errors.meaning: Value for ts was missing or invalid.
errors.fix: Pass the parent message's ts, not a reply's.

errors.meaning: Value for channel was missing or invalid.
The request was rate limited.
errors.fix: Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then retry.

calls.body: The docs list form-encoded only for this method, so the example sends query parameters, not JSON.

calls.summary: Find a workspace user by email address.

auth.notes: users:read alone no longer returns the email field. Custom bot users can't use this method.

errors.meaning: No user found for the email. Also returned for deactivated users.
The token is not granted the scope this call needs.
errors.fix: Add users:read.email and reinstall.

calls.summary: Read recent messages from a channel.

params.notes: Tool name from Slack's official slack-skills-plugin repo. oldest and latest are message timestamps that bound the window. Slack's commands use limits of 50 to 100. The channel argument's name isn't stated (get the ID from slack_search_channels); read it from tools/list.

auth.notes: OAuth sign-in to your workspace on first use, as you. A workspace admin must approve MCP integration first. Slack's server doesn't support dynamic client registration, so the client needs a Slack-registered OAuth client ID; Slack's official plugins for Claude Code and Cursor carry one.

config.generic:
{ "mcpServers": { "slack": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.slack.com/mcp" } } }
# Plus the OAuth client ID your client is registered with Slack under. See auth notes.

platforms.claude-code:
/plugin marketplace add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin
/plugin install slack@slack

errors.meaning: Sign-in can't finish until a workspace admin approves MCP integration, per Slack's plugin README.
errors.fix: Ask a workspace admin to approve the Slack MCP integration, then sign in again.

calls.notes: Slack's docs say the MCP connection works in Claude Code and Cursor; in Codex the plugin installs skills only.

smoke.notes: Checks tools/list includes the tool, the way Slack's own eval tests do (Bearer token on a Streamable HTTP session). Needs a user OAuth token from a Slack MCP sign-in.
